The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned because it brings the narrator's internal arc to a meaningful resolution by weaving together the motifs established earlier in the story. Throughout the piece, the narrator observes his mother's routines and his late father's unfinished tasks—most notably the broken garage gutter. After his mother's hospitalization forces him to confront her mortality and recognize that her "habits" were actually an act of loving maintenance to keep their family world intact for him, he decides to take on that maintenance himself. By recalling the story of the water buckets, the "held note" of the house, and finally resolving to learn how to fix the gutter, the narrator reaches the exact emotional and thematic realization the entire story has been building toward.
